annotation.title_clean: Regulating sidewalk delivery robots as a disruptive new urban technology
annotation.title_en: Regulating sidewalk delivery robots as a disruptive new urban technology
annotation.authors_or_issuer: Kovacic, M.; Marvin, S.; While, A.
annotation.summary_en: Journal article analysing how California municipalities regulate sidewalk delivery robots, identifying prohibitive, permissive and collaborative approaches. Based on policy analysis and interviews, it shows first-mover firms like Starship shaped permitting, with liability and insurance burdens falling on operators.
key_provisions_or_claims: California cities adopted prohibitive, permissive and collaborative sidewalk robot regulation.
First-mover firms such as Starship strongly shaped permitting rules, including state legislation in 2019.
Palo Alto requires encroachment permits, operator liability, $2-4M insurance and 24-hour reporting of significant collisions.
Semi-enclosed campus and precinct trials act as test beds for single-company development.
Sidewalk robots are disruptive because their safety is unproven in complex public space.
